messages:
Maya (Acme): Hey team — we're seeing intermittent parse failures from JSON mode on /v1/generate. Happens when we send an array of items with nested 'metadata' objects. Parser throws 'Unexpected end of input' or complains about missing required fields for some array items. Also noticed a couple 401s earlier today and a short spike in latency. Can we triage?

Jia (support): Sorry you're hitting this, Maya. Can you paste a minimal request + the response that failed (raw)? Also which model and are you using streaming?

Maya (Acme): We are using model: 'redwood-2-large', streaming: true, structured_output: true. Minimal request below (redacted keys):

```json
POST /v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\nBody:
{
  "json_mode": "structured",
  "prompt": "...",
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "items": [
    {"name": "alpha", "metadata": {"id": 123, "tags": ["a"]}},
    {"name": "beta", "metadata": {"tags": ["b"]}},
    {"name": "gamma", "metadata": {"id": 125, "tags": ["c"]}}
  ]
}
```

Maya (Acme): Failing response (stream chunked) — parser fails on item 2. Raw stream snippet: 

```
{"items":[{"name":"alpha","metadata":{"id":123,"tags":["a"]}},{"name":"beta","metadata":{"tags":["b"]}},{"name":"gamma","metadata":{"id":125,"tags":["c"]}}]}

# but we received chunks like:
{"items":[{"name":"alpha","metadata":{"id":123,"tags":["a"]}},{"name":"beta","metadata":{"tags
":{"b"]}},{"name":"gamma","metadata":{"id":125,"tags":["c"]}}]}
```

Maya (Acme): parser fails because the stream split within the 'tags' array for item 2, produced invalid JSON. Expected to tolerate chunk boundaries.

Jia (support): Thanks — that looks like a streaming boundary break. Two quick asks: 1) can you attach the request_id from response headers for one failing request? 2) can you reproduce with streaming disabled? That helps narrow to chunking vs model output content.

Maya (Acme): request-id: req_0a7f3c. Repro with streaming=false reduces failures but not completely (we still get occasional items missing 'id'). Not always correlated with streaming.

OpsBot: automatic note: service-deploy v2026-03-04 rolled at 02:11 UTC to all inference nodes.

Ethan (eng): Looping in eng. From the snippet it looks like two issues: 1) stream-chunk boundary may split UTF or token boundaries causing truncated/invalid JSON in the client stream; 2) schema drift/partial items — some items are returned without required 'id' field. We're seeing a small rate of 'partial-object' logs in runtime (0.06% overall) starting around that deploy window.

Ethan (eng): Can you run this quick repro loop for 10 requests with streaming=true and capture the raw socket stream (or the SSE frames)? Also include the full response headers. We'll correlate with req_0a7f3c in logs.

Anika (billing): Noticed some 401/402s in that hour from the same tenant due to a temporary KMS rotation and billing fallback. Not sure if that causes trimmed responses, but when we fall back to the 'restricted' key the gateway will return truncated results with a short error frame in-stream. I'll check the timeline.

Maya (Acme): Ok we captured 10 attempts and attached logs to the ticket (link). Failures: 3/10 with invalid JSON stream boundary; 1/10 with valid JSON but item 2 missing 'id' entirely (schema violation). No 401s in these traces.

Jia (support): Useful. From support side: two mitigation suggestions you can try immediately: 1) set request header `X-Redwood-Strict-Json: true` to opt into a server-side generator that emits complete objects per SSE frame (reduces streaming chunk splits), 2) as a fallback set `json_mode` to 'lenient' and post-process to validate items and request retries for missing required fields. Both require app changes but can buy time.

Ethan (eng): Internally: we found a bug in the SSE framing when using continuous batching + prefix caching — in edge cases the last SSE frame for a batch could be emitted without a closing newline which some client decoders treat as truncated. Fix: ensure final frame terminator is emitted and a small backpressure delay (2ms) when flushing batch end. We're patching now and will roll canary tomorrow.

Ethan (eng): For the missing 'id' field: looks like model output sometimes omits optional tokens when using sampling + top_p. In a few cases the 'metadata' subobject is emitted incomplete (model-level output variance). We should add a server-side post-validate step for structured outputs to drop/mark incomplete items. I'll open an internal ticket to add strict validation with an option to fail the entire response vs emit partials.

Anika (billing): Regarding the earlier 401s — I confirmed a brief KMS rotation at 2026-03-04T02:10:45 UTC that caused ~2m of auth retries for a small percentage of requests. We reverted the fallback policy; full auth stability restored at 02:13. Unclear this affected your specific req_0a7f3c, but tagging the events on the logs now.

Maya (Acme): Appreciate the quick triage. Two clarifying Qs: 1) Will the streaming framing patch guarantee no split inside JSON tokens? 2) For server-side validation, can we opt-in to failing the whole request so we don't have to handle partial items?

Ethan (eng): 1) Patch reduces but cannot absolutely guarantee client-level decoding errors (net proxies can still split). It makes SSE frames token-aligned at emitter side which eliminates our contributor to the splits. 2) We'll add an API flag `structured_validation=fail_on_partial` that you can set; if validation fails we'll return a 500 with a validation error rather than emit partial items. ETA for canary: 48h; broad rollout 1 week, unless blocked in testing.

Jia (support): Action items: - Maya: try `X-Redwood-Strict-Json: true` and capture results. - Maya: include raw SSE frames for any failing case and attach headers (req id). - Eng: track canary and patch for SSE terminator and add server-side validation ticket. - Billing: annotate logs for KMS rotation window and confirm no further fallbacks.

Maya (Acme): Will try the strict header and report back. Thanks. :thumbsup:

OpsBot: ticket TKT-4521 created: 'support: nested-json partial items + stream splits' assigned to Ethan, Jia. Priority: P2.
